shots.say: Who looks after baby Tumble?
Just his mama? Or lots of elephants?
I'm Milo. Let's find out together!
Welcome to The Animated Zoo, friends!
Today we fly to the sunny savanna.
Here we are! Look who is waiting for us.
This is Tumble. A baby elephant is called a calf.
Who looks after Tumble? Mama does, every day!
Tumble walks over and stays close to Mama.
Baby elephants stick close to their mamas.
Where is Tumble? Far away, or close to Mama?
Close to Mama! Close, close, close.
Mama touches Tumble with her trunk, again and again.
Can you give yourself a big hug? Squeeze!
Tumble is hungry. What does a baby elephant drink?
Water, or milk? What do you think?
Milk! Tumble drinks his mama's milk.
Does he drink it with his trunk, or with his mouth?
With his mouth! A baby elephant drinks milk with its mouth.
So he does not need a long trunk yet.
Tumble's trunk is short and wobbly. Wiggle, wobble!
Is Tumble's trunk long, or short?
Short! Short and wobbly, for now.
At first, a calf is clumsy with its trunk.
But it learns to use its trunk as it grows.
Can you wiggle your arm like a wobbly trunk? Wiggle, wiggle!
Tumble drinks Mama's milk many times a day.
Mama looks after Tumble. But is Mama the only one?
Here comes Tumble's family. This is the herd!
A herd is a family: mamas, aunties, big sisters and babies.
This is Auntie. Hello, Auntie!
And this is Tumble's big sister.
Who is the smallest elephant here? Tumble, or Auntie?
Tumble! He is the baby of the herd.
Let's count them. One, two, three!
Auntie says hello. She touches Tumble with her trunk.
Does Auntie say hello with her trunk, or with her tail?
With her trunk! Pat, pat. Hello, Tumble!
Can you wave hello like a trunk? Hello, hello!
Big sister plays with Tumble. Push, push, play!
Helpers like Auntie and big sister are like babysitters.
They watch Tumble, they help him, and they play with him.
And Mama can eat her grass. Munch, munch!
How many helpers are with Tumble? One, or two?
Two! Auntie and big sister.
When Tumble was born, he stood up in just minutes.
Mama and the other elephants helped him up.
Can you stand up tall like Tumble? Stand up, stand tall!
Lots of helpers! But who leads the whole herd?
Meet Grandma. She is the oldest elephant in the herd.
Grandma is the leader of the herd.
The leader is the oldest female. She knows the most.
Who leads the herd? Tumble, or Grandma?
Grandma! Everyone follows Grandma.
Grandma leads the herd to water and food.
Follow the leader! Step, step, step.
Grandma decides when to walk, and when to stop.
Can you march like an elephant? Stomp, stomp, stomp!
Here is the river. Grandma knew the way!
Grandma has a long, cool drink. Slurp!
How many elephants are in Tumble's family? Let's count!
One, two, three, four, five!
Five! Grandma, Mama, Auntie, big sister and Tumble.
Elephants can make a low rumble. It means: everything is okay.
Can you make a low rumble? Rumble, rumble!
The sun goes down. Grandma says it is time to rest.
Tumble rests close to Mama. Cozy and happy!
Who looks after Tumble? Only Mama, or the whole family?
The whole family! Mama, Auntie, big sister and Grandma.
Big family, big love. Wow!
Time to remember what we learned!
How does Tumble drink his milk? With his trunk, or his mouth?
With his mouth!
Who leads the herd? Tumble, or Grandma?
Grandma, the oldest!
And who helps Mama look after Tumble?
Auntie and big sister, the helpers!
Good night, Tumble. Good night, Mama.
Thank you for learning with me, friends. See you at the zoo!
